pron_note: chào: huyền tone, low and relaxed; em: mid, flat
anh: short a plus n at the teeth, [ăn]; the final is not the ng of ăn
en: Hi. (what a younger person says to you)

pron_note: khỏe: dip then rise, like a Mandarin 3rd tone; không is often "hông" in casual Saigon speech
dạ: d is y in Saigon, as in English yes; nặng tone. To your father you open the answer with dạ and call yourself con. Hanoi also uses vâng, rare in Saigon
rất: r curled back like the Mandarin 日, and the final t is said as c (rấc). The voice says z here, which is wrong 錄音的 r 不對，你要唸捲舌的「日」。
ăn sounds like "ăng" in Saigon
en: Have you eaten yet? (a common way to greet)
zh: 你吃飯了沒？（常見的打招呼）

pron_note: the answer to Anh ăn cơm chưa?: rồi = already, 了
ngang tone: flat, mid, no movement (lower than a Mandarin 1st tone)
en: (ngang) older brother, you; younger sibling, you; eat; go; name
zh: （ngang）哥哥、你；弟弟妹妹、你；吃；去；名字

pron_note: huyền tone: low, falling gently, relaxed voice
en: (huyền) to be; and; house; what; person

pron_note: sắc tone: rising, like a Mandarin 2nd tone; on biết it is short and high
en: (sắc) have; fish; speak; know; morning, bright

pron_note: hỏi and ngã are one tone in Saigon: dip then rise, like a full Mandarin 3rd tone, longer than the others
en: (hỏi / ngã) healthy; ask; be at, live; also; more, again

pron_note: nặng tone: low, falling, a slight rise at the end; on mệt, học, một, được it is short, cut off by the final consonant
en: (nặng) tired; study; one; can, get; older sister, you

pron_note: one syllable, five Saigon tones: level, low falling, rising, dip-rise, low with a slight rise
en: ghost; but, that; mom (Saigon); code; rice seedling
zh: 鬼；但是、而；媽（南部）；代碼；秧苗

pron_note: bả = bà ấy, she (colloquial Southern)
zh: 三、爸（南部）；奶奶、太太；她（口語）

pron_note: cỡ đó (about that much) is colloquial Southern
en: muscle; flag, chess; reason, pretext (cái cớ); size, roughly (cỡ đó)
zh: 肌肉；旗、棋；藉口；大小、大概

pron_note: ă: short and clipped; â: short and central, like the e in German "bitte"; a: long and open
in Saigon the final -n here sounds like -ng: lang, lăng, lâng
o: open, like German "offen"; ô: closed, like "Ofen"; ơ: unrounded, like the vowel in English "bird", long; â is its short partner
en: big; big bowl, e.g. for phở (a rice bowl is chén in Saigon, bát in Hanoi); silk
zh: 大；大碗（裝河粉的碗；飯碗南部說 chén）；絲

en: worry; lot, plot (lô đất); ignore (lơ đi)

pron_note: ư: say u but spread the lips as for i

en: practise (religion); private, personal (tư nhân); also four, fourth (thứ Tư, chú Tư)
zh: 修行；私（tư nhân 私人）；四（thứ Tư 星期三）

pron_note: e: open, like German "Bett"; ê: closed, like "Beet"

en: sweet soup; criticise, look down on

pron_note: bé: in Saigon a little kid; small is nhỏ (Hanoi: bé). bế is Northern; Saigon says bồng or ẵm
en: small, little kid; carry (a child) in the arms

pron_note: ia: i gliding into a lazy ơ; written iê before a final consonant, same sound
ua: u gliding into ơ; written uô before a final
ưa: ư gliding into ơ; written ươ before a final
quá: keep the k, kwá. In Saigon you will often hear wá in fast speech. Hanoi also says kwá 唸 kwá，不要唸成 wá。
en: The weather is so nice and cool.

vi: Cho anh một ly cà phê sữa đá.
pron_note: ly = glass (Saigon; Hanoi: cốc); một ends with the lips closed, like "mộc"
en: One iced milk coffee, please. (literally: give me one glass of ...)
zh: 我要一杯冰的煉乳咖啡。

pron_note: chưa at the end asks whether something has happened yet, like 了嗎
en: Do you know yet? / Have you heard?
Not yet, I don't know yet.

vi: dạ, dài, dễ, gì, giờ, giá
pron_note: d and gi are both y (as in English yes) in Saigon
en: yes (polite); long; easy; what; hour, time; price
zh: 是、嗯；長；容易；什麼；點、時間；價格

pron_note: đ is a real d, tongue at the teeth, with a slight inward gulp (implosive); a plain d is fine
y versus d
en: long; station, platform (đài truyền hình = TV station)

pron_note: say v. In fast Saigon speech and in much of the Mekong Delta you will hear y (vui like yui). Hanoi says v
en: happy; return, go home; so, like that; and

pron_note: Saigon r: tongue curled back, close to an English r, not the Hanoi z. the voice says z here and that is wrong: you say the Mandarin 日, tongue curled back 錄音的 r 不對，你要唸捲舌的 日
en: already; go out; very; cheap; wash

pron_note: three spellings, two sounds in Saigon: ra with r, da and gia both with y. the voice says z here and that is wrong: you say the Mandarin 日, tongue curled back 錄音的 r 不對，你要唸捲舌的 日
zh: 出去；皮膚；家（gia đình 家庭）

pron_note: tr: tongue curled back. ch: tongue flat behind the teeth. Keeping them apart is the careful Saigon form; fast Saigon speech and Hanoi merge them. the voice merges tr and ch here and that is the fast Saigon form: you keep them apart 錄音把 tr 和 ch 混在一起了，你要分開唸
same pair on another vowel. the voice merges tr and ch here and that is the fast Saigon form: you keep them apart 錄音把 tr 和 ch 混在一起了，你要分開唸
con trai = son, cái chai = the bottle. The whole meaning hangs on tr against ch. the voice merges tr and ch here and that is the fast Saigon form: you keep them apart 錄音把 tr 和 ch 混在一起了，你要分開唸

say them apart: s with the tongue curled back like Mandarin 是, x like a plain s. Both end like ưn (sưn, xưn), the vowel pulls back. Fast Saigon speech and Hanoi merge s and x. xinh itself is Northern-flavoured; in Saigon say đẹp or dễ thương. The voice merges s and x and misses the vowel trace: you keep them apart 錄音把 s 和 x 混在一起了，你要分開唸。
same pair, other order. the voice merges s and x here and that is the fast Saigon form: you keep them apart 錄音把 s 和 x 混在一起了，你要分開唸
t = Mandarin d (no puff of air); th = Mandarin t (puff of air)
c = Mandarin g; kh = Mandarin k, aspirated (Hanoi adds friction, like the ch in German "Bach")

say kw: quá, quê, quen, quán, the k stays. That is the careful Saigon form; your tandem may well say wá, wê, wen, wán, which is everyday Saigon speech. Hanoi also says kw, so this is about care, not about dialect 唸 kw。西貢日常常說 wá，這是講究程度，不是南北差別。
en: too, very; hometown, countryside; be used to, know (someone); shop, café, eatery
zh: 太、非常；家鄉；熟悉、認識；店、館

pron_note: ng at the start of a syllable: the sound at the end of "sing", then keep going
nh: Spanish ñ, the ny in "canyon"
en: house; many, much; miss, remember; fast

pron_note: ph = f
g, gh: a soft g with friction, like the g in Spanish "amigo"
ừ: the casual yes to a friend or someone younger; dạ is what they say to you. hiểu rồi = got it

en: What are we having for lunch today?

pron_note: bự = big, colloquial Southern; lớn is the neutral word; Hanoi mostly to

vi: Người Sài Gòn nói nhanh quá.

pron_note: nha: soft Southern particle for requests and friendly statements, like 喔 or 吧
cổ = cô ấy (she), Saigon contraction; Hanoi and formal speech: cô ấy
four finals: -m, -n, -ng, -nh. In Saigon làn sounds like làng, and lành like lằn: short a, n at the teeth
en: do, work; lane; village; benign, gentle

pron_note: not the same word. The final is n in both, but the vowel differs: tin has a clear i, tinh pulls the vowel back toward ư, so it sounds like tưn. The palatal nh is gone in Saigon, yet it leaves its trace in the vowel, exactly as anh becomes ăn. Fast speech flattens the difference, careful speech keeps it. Hanoi keeps them apart by the final, n against nh. 不是同一個字：尾音都是 n，母音不同，tinh 的母音偏 ư。The voice says both alike, which is the fast Saigon form: you pull the vowel back. 錄音兩個唸一樣，你要把母音往後拉。
zh: 相信、消息；精（tinh thần 精神）

pron_note: same rule as tin and tinh: chín has a clear i, chính pulls the vowel toward ư. The n at the end is the same in both. This is the careful Saigon difference, not a Northern one: Hanoi keeps the difference in the final consonant instead, n against nh. 母音不同：chính 偏 ư，尾音都是 n。The voice says both alike, which is the fast Saigon form: you pull the vowel back. 錄音兩個唸一樣，你要把母音往後拉。
these two really are the same in Saigon: after o, ô, u a final t turns into a k and the lips close. That is a Southern feature, not carelessness, and it stays. Hanoi keeps t and c apart
really the same in Saigon: after ă a final t turns into a k. A Southern feature, not carelessness, and it stays; Hanoi keeps t and c apart
really the same in Saigon: after iê a final t turns into a k. A Southern feature, not carelessness, and it stays; Hanoi keeps t and c apart
en: regret, pity (tiếc quá); period, section (tiết học); tiết kiệm = save, economise
zh: 可惜；節（tiết học 一節課；tiết kiệm 節儉、節省）

pron_note: tập: the lips close and stay closed; tất: in Saigon a k, like tấc; tách: a cut t with a short a, [tắt]. No puff of air, no release
en: practise; all (tất cả; for socks Saigon says vớ, Hanoi tất); cup
zh: 練習；全部（tất cả；襪子南部說 vớ，北部說 tất）；杯子

pron_note: all four end in a stopped consonant; such syllables only take the sắc or nặng tone
after o, ô, u as the whole vowel, the final -ng closes the lips as well, like "ngm": không, ông, đúng. In uống the vowel is uô and ends open, so the lips do not close
en: no, not; grandfather, Mr; correct; drink

pron_note: after o, ô, u the final -c closes the lips too: like "kp"
en: study; read; lump, piece; speed (tốc độ)
zh: 學；讀；塊；速（tốc độ 速度）

pron_note: -anh in Saigon: short a plus n at the teeth, [ăn]; -ach: short a plus a cut t, [ăt]
en: older brother, you; blue, green; fast; guest, customer

pron_note: -ênh and -êch in Saigon: the palatal final becomes n and t, and the vowel pulls back toward ơ, so bệnh sounds close to bợn. You say bệnh; you will hear bịnh in the South, especially from older speakers. Hanoi keeps a clear ê and a palatal final. The voice keeps a clear ê here: you pull the vowel toward ơ 錄音的 ê 太清楚，你要把母音往 ơ 拉。

vi: một, hai, ba, bốn, năm, sáu, bảy, tám, chín, mười
pron_note: một sounds like mộc, bốn like bống, chín keeps a clear i; năm and tám end in m; you will hear mừi for mười
ăn sounds like "ăng"
mắc = expensive, Southern; Hanoi: đắt

vi: Em nói được tiếng Anh không?
Anh là giáo viên tiếng Đức.
Anh dạy tiếng Đức cho người Trung Quốc.
pron_note: người Trung Quốc = from China; người Hoa = ethnic Chinese in general, also the Chinese-Vietnamese in Saigon
en: I teach German to Chinese people.

pron_note: ba = dad, Southern; Hanoi: bố

vi: Má anh là người Trung Quốc.
pron_note: má = mom, Southern; Hanoi: mẹ
in Saigon "tiếng Hoa" is just as common for the Chinese language

en: Where are you? / Where do you live?

pron_note: hả: question particle for checking or mild surprise, like 喔 or 是嗎

en: What do you do for a living?

pron_note: ổng = ông ấy (he, an older man), Saigon contraction; Hanoi and formal speech: ông ấy. About your own father it sounds casual, fine with friends, cheeky in front of older people
ảnh = anh ấy (he), Saigon contraction; Hanoi and formal speech: anh ấy
thiệt: say this (Southern); Hanoi and writing: thật

en: Okay, I'm going to sleep now.

pron_note: nghen: warm Southern particle, softer than nha; it sounds older or Mekong and fits your father; with tandems nha is the usual choice
